chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Karkhi, from al-Hasan ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Then give them a gift and send them away with a fair release.' He said: 'Give them a gift, beautify them with what you are able of goodness, for they return with sadness and fear and great worry and admiration from their enemies. Indeed, Allah is Generous, He is bashful (of His glory) and loves those who are modest. The most noble of you is the one who is most eager to honor his wives.'

As for that which indicates that the gift (mut'ah) for those not yet entered into is obligatory, it is His, Exalted is He, saying: 'No blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or prescribed for them a dowry, but give them a gift, upon the wealthy according to his means and upon the poor according to his means, a provision in fairness, a right upon the doers of good.'
So He commanded the gift for whoever divorces before entering with the woman, and His command, Exalted, is upon obligation, and also it has been narrated.

key_terms.مَتْعَةٌ: Gift or provision given to a divorced wife

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on giving a gift to a wife divorced before consummation?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the command to 'entertain them well' as a moral imperative to alleviate the emotional distress and social stigma a woman faces upon returning to her family. It further establishes the legal obligation of mut'ah (gift) for those divorced before consummation, linking the divine command to the practical reality of the husband's financial capacity, thereby reinforcing the Shia jurisprudential view on post-divorce rights.
